When asked what protects the safety of EVs and large-scale storage batteries, many people might think of a BMS (Battery Management System).
The BMS is the 'brain' that monitors voltage and temperature to detect abnormalities.
However, detecting an abnormality is not the same as reliably stopping dangerous current.
When a large current flows due to a short circuit or similar event, there is a final safety component that physically disconnects the circuit.
That is the fuse.
Hello everyone, this is MoneyGolem.
The company I am introducing this time, Littelfuse (NASDAQ: LFUS), is a US company that, true to its name, started with fuses and has expanded its business into semiconductors, sensors, relays, and contactors.
Fuses are small and usually appear to be doing nothing.
However, at the moment an accident occurs, they blow themselves to stop the current in order to protect the battery, wiring, inverter, and people.
Even in production technology, safety components cannot simply be 'good if they are cheap.' This is because it is necessary to prove through design and evaluation that they operate reliably during an abnormality and do not malfunction during normal operation.
This time, we will look at Littelfuse not just as a small component manufacturer, but as a company that sells 'physical safety devices' that are the last line of defense to stop abnormal current in battery systems.
1. What kind of company is Littelfuse?
Littelfuse is a circuit protection, power control, and sensing manufacturer founded in 1927.
The business is broadly divided into three areas: electronics, transportation, and industrial equipment.
Representative products are as follows:
Overvoltage protection components such as TVS diodes
Sensors for temperature, position, current, etc.
In the battery sector, we have touchpoints in EV battery packs, high-voltage power distribution units, onboard chargers, inverters, and stationary energy storage systems.
High-voltage DC fuses are a particularly clear example.
When battery cells are connected in series, the system voltage rises from several hundred volts to over 1,000V. The stored energy also increases, and in the event of a short circuit, a very large current can flow.
Littelfuse offers 1,000Vdc-rated fuses for EVs and products with a breaking capacity of 1,500Vdc and up to 250kA for battery storage systems.
As batteries grow into larger systems—from cells to modules, racks, and PCS—the importance of circuit protection also increases.
Littelfuse is not a battery manufacturing company.
However, we are a company that transforms the large energy stored in batteries into a state where it can be used safely.
2. Why is a fuse necessary if there is a BMS?
A BMS monitors the battery's voltage, current, temperature, and more.
When it detects an abnormality, it instructs the contactor to "cut the circuit."
So, is having a BMS and a contactor enough?
In actual safety design, we even consider cases where the control system does not function normally.
The sensor cannot correctly detect abnormal values
The control signal does not reach its destination
The contactor contacts weld shut and will not open
A short-circuit current exceeding expectations flows all at once
In such cases, the fuse melts its internal metal at a certain current level or higher, physically disconnecting the circuit.
In other words, if the BMS is the "brain that considers abnormalities," the fuse is the safety valve that finally cuts the current path.
Moreover, cutting high-voltage direct current is not easy.

Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE) stock rose 9% to $1,058.42, while Corning (NYSE:GLW) stock advanced 3% to $158.89.
The broader optics rally outpaced the market. The Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF (CBOE:LYTE) gained 4% to $25.40, while the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) slipped 0.2% to $761.11.
Coherent introduced PhotonLink in September as an integrated-optics platform for next-generation AI data centers. The company also expanded its Pluggable Optical Line System portfolio, linking chip-to-chip, inside-the-rack, and high-capacity data-center connectivity products to the same AI infrastructure buildout.
PhotonLink highlights Coherent’s vertically integrated position across materials, lasers, optics, specialty fibers, and related manufacturing capabilities. Coherent said the platform includes more than 10 customer engagements for co-packaged optics and more than 10 customer engagements for near-packaged optics.
AI data centers require more bandwidth and more efficient connections as workloads become larger and more complex. Coherent could benefit if hyperscalers and equipment makers accelerate deployments of advanced optical components, though the company must turn early engagement into sustained orders and profitable production.
Bernstein initiated coverage of Coherent with an Outperform rating as part of broader coverage of U.S. networking and optical companies. Bernstein said networking and optical suppliers could be “structural winners” within AI infrastructure, an assessment that helped reinforce investor interest in Coherent stock.
The research firm also began coverage of Lumentum, Ciena Corporation (NYSE:CIEN), and Arista Networks (NYSE:ANET) with Outperform ratings. Bernstein initiated Cisco Systems (NASDAQ:CSCO) and Corning with Market Perform ratings, providing a more balanced view of an industry that has rallied sharply on AI-related expectations.
Coherent stock’s 10% gain exceeded the 4% move in the LYTE ETF, suggesting that PhotonLink and Bernstein’s favorable initiation gave traders a company-specific reason to bid up the shares. Still, Coherent stock can remain sensitive to shifts in AI capital-spending expectations, customer order timing, and concerns about industry capacity.
Lumentum stock climbed 9% to $1,058.42, extending the recovery that began after a recent optics-sector selloff. Lumentum reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $1.006 billion, up 109.3% year over year, while adjusted earnings per share of $3.23 exceeded the $2.97 consensus estimate.
The company guided for fiscal first-quarter revenue between $1.225 billion and $1.275 billion. Lumentum management said demand signals for 2027 remained “incredibly strong,” while the company also reported that optical-circuit-switch shipments doubled from the fiscal third quarter to the fiscal fourth quarter.
